executionHistory.summary: Created one consolidated packet after reconciling Specs 068, 069, 071, and 076; confirmed required scenarios are current; statically confirmed compiler-disabled test config, missing production compiler wiring and ML route, state-machine response gaps, five t.Skipf bailouts, and missing generic guard coverage. No implementation or live tests were run.

Implemented product-owned Scopes 1 and 2 plus implementation-adjacent strict required tests. Go/Python units, focused live integration, exact five required E2E, full assistant E2E, check, lint, format, artifact lint, traceability, and installed regression guard passed. Scopes remain in_progress because planning-owned concrete path reconciliation and the upstream Bubbles Go skip-family guard remain open; certification was not modified.

Regression phase executed against the packet's own subject: do the tests covering this fix bind their claims? ONE mutation check on the guard that closes the named root cause (compiler-disabled test config). Baseline at clean HEAD: focused unit selector on TestIntentCompilerRequiredWhenAssistantHTTPEnabled exited 0 in 96s wall with internal/config reporting 0.091s (executed, not 'no tests to run'). Mutation: the F069-INTENT-COMPILER-DISABLED coherence check in internal/config/assistant.go was disabled by short-circuiting its condition. Mutated run FAILED exactly as required — '--- FAIL: TestIntentCompilerRequiredWhenAssistantHTTPEnabled' with 'enabled transport with compiler disabled error = <nil>, want F069-INTENT-COMPILER-DISABLED'. Restored with an explicit git checkout as its own step; porcelain verified empty and the guard condition verified present at line 556. Post-restore run exited 0 in 64s. The test therefore binds its claim: removing the fix kills it. Direct grep across all five manifest-required assistant test files found zero t.Skip/t.Skipf/t.SkipNow, and the two bare returns present sit in non-required negative-invariant tests exiting on a false antecedent, not on a failure condition. Adversarial probe recorded a real limitation: regression-quality-guard.sh reports 0 violations on a throwaway file containing nothing but t.Skip and t.Skipf, and its source contains zero skip-family tokens, so its clean result on the five required files is a blind pass rather than skip-freeness evidence. tests/e2e/agent/no_skip_guard_test.go enforces no-skip but scans only its own directory without recursing, so it does not cover tests/e2e/assistant. Skip-freeness is therefore true by content today and mechanically unguarded, which reinforces the already-open TR-BUG-069-005-FRAMEWORK-001 rather than opening a new route. No source file was modified on exit; no DoD item was checked; no certification field was written.

DELIVERED: tests/e2e/assistant/required_no_skip_guard_test.go (commit 673bb6a073062287d52db53d531bcc62534ba906), a no-skip guard bound to the five manifest-required assistant E2E identities. It is a DENYLIST keyed to those five names, not a directory-wide no-skip rule, because tests/e2e/assistant carries roughly thirty legitimate t.Skip/t.Skipf calls across twenty-one files (live-stack guards, environment branches, planned placeholders) and a blanket rule would be both wrong and immediately red. Skip detection is function-body scoped through go/parser rather than brace counting, because these files embed JSON string literals whose braces would desynchronize a counter. A MISSING required test is FATAL rather than a silent pass, so deleting a required identity cannot quietly satisfy the guard. Seven named adversarial subtests prove the guard can fail. Also delivered in this run: the four artifact-gate repairs recorded in report.md, and the two state.json routing/claim repairs recorded here. NOT DELIVERED, and deliberately so: no product runtime behavior changed. The guard is test-surface only, adds no production code path, and does not repair the upstream framework gap; regression-quality-guard.sh still contains zero skip-family tokens and still cannot detect Go skips, which is why TR-BUG-069-005-FRAMEWORK-001 remains open. runStartedAt is the measured commit time of this invocation's repository-binding decision rb:vscode-...:4, not a reconstructed session start; runDurationSeconds is omitted because the true end of the run postdates this write and no honest single measurement spans it. No DoD box was checked, no certification field was written, and status remains in_progress.

Checked 8 DoD items across Scopes 1-3. Left the validate-owned certification item unchecked; Scope 3 stays In Progress because of it.

Simplify phase over the two commits carrying this packet's code. PART 1, e4618e8e: reviewed AS LANDED and NOT re-executed in this run. That commit was produced by an earlier simplify-phase run whose code landed but whose phase claim was never written, which is the reason this claim was missing. Reading its diff shows it is broader than the parameter drop alone: it (a) removed the unused conv parameter from proposeCompiledAction, (b) extracted enforceCompiledWeatherProvenance collapsing three identical provenance.Enforce blocks, (c) extracted a rejectChoice closure collapsing two identical response-build-and-persist blocks in resolveCompilerDisambig, and (d) STRENGTHENED assertCompiledWeatherHonestFailure to assert response.Body == provenance.CanonicalRefusalBody. Item (d) is the one that matters here: the helper previously checked status and error-cause fields only, so a response whose body still read as a capture acknowledgement satisfied every field it examined and passed - the same false-green defect class this packet documents. All four were re-reviewed and kept; no evidence in this record rests on re-running them. PART 2, 673bb6a0: tests/e2e/assistant/required_no_skip_guard_test.go was the only substantial un-reviewed source, and three behaviour-preserving simplifications were applied to it. S1 removed the dead 'c := c' loop-variable copy (go.mod declares go 1.25.10 and Go has had per-iteration loop scoping since 1.22; confirmed the only such statement in the directory). S2 replaced strconv.Itoa(line) under a %s verb with %d on the int, retiring the now-unused strconv import. S3 removed a temp-file write-then-read round trip from the adversarial subtest: scanRequiredTestBodyForSkips takes src []byte and never opens the path, so the round trip reproduced []byte(c.body) at the cost of two error branches irrelevant to the code under test; the fixture is now passed in memory, which also makes the file's own isolation rationale stronger rather than weaker, and both doc comments asserting the old temp-directory rationale were corrected. ZERO assertions were removed, relaxed or narrowed in this phase; the seven wantSkips/wantMissing expectations are untouched and still execute. VERIFIED, not assumed: 'test unit --go --go-run' over both guard tests exits 0 with 'go test ./... finished OK', which is the whole-module build proof after the import change. Execution was proven separately from the exit code because an exit 0 under a -run selector can be vacuous - the target package line reads 'ok github.com/smackerel/smackerel/tests/e2e/assistant 0.014s' with NO '[no tests to run]' marker while every other package in the same run carries one, and a verbose re-run yields an individual --- PASS line for both tests and all seven adversarial subtests. No file was deleted, so the deletion-safety gate did not apply. No architectural change was implied, so no design or planning route was raised. runDurationSeconds is omitted rather than invented. No DoD box was checked - the single remaining unchecked item names bubbles.validate as its actor. certification.certifiedCompletedPhases was not touched and status remains in_progress.
